intro: The Oracle at Delphi has stopped answering questions; instead she has left a set of riddles, each one sworn upon a different god, and the pilgrim crowd now waits with tablets rather than requests. Along the temple wall hangs a rack of bronze slots, each one filed to a different width, and the custom forming among the suppliants is to solve a riddle and then slide its answer strip into the slot that takes it snugly. A strip forced into a wider slot is treated as the work of a careless seer, and a strip left beside the rack counts for nothing. Beneath every slot runs a narrow channel, and at the bottom of each channel someone has fixed a letter in dark pitch. The pilgrims say the pitch letters matter only when each slot holds exactly the length it was made for; then, they believe, the letters will speak in the Pythia's place.
echo: The gods live nearly three thousand metres up, above the clouds of Thessaly.

puzzles.title: Elysian Fields
puzzles.flavor: A strip of paper tape, seven holes wide, fed through the teletype at Delphi.
hints: Each row of the paper tape is a 7-bit ASCII character (hole = 1, most significant bit on the left).
To check you're on track: the answer begins with P.

puzzles.title: Know Thyself
puzzles.flavor: Not a single letter on the page, and yet it says something.
hints: Each symbol stands for one letter (a simple substitution); word breaks are kept. Solve the sentence; it tells you the answer.
To check you're on track: the answer begins with A.

puzzles.title: The Golden Fleece
puzzles.flavor: Julius would have read this before breakfast.

blocks.text: KSZZ RCBS MCI AOM BCK KFWHS RCKB HVS KCFR VSFASG OBR ACJS EIWSHZM CB HC HVS BSLH CBS

hints: Every letter of the sentence was shifted along the alphabet by the same amount. Find the shift; the sentence tells you the answer.
To check you're on track: the answer begins with H.

puzzles.title: Twelve Labours
puzzles.flavor: A pub quiz where every answer is a count. Keep a tally, then keep counting.

items: Guns fired in a traditional royal salute
Suits in a deck of cards
Holes on a full golf course
Red balls racked at the start of a snooker frame

hints: Each line is a number from 1 to 26. Turn each number into a letter (A = 1, B = 2, …).
To check you're on track: the answer begins with T.

puzzles.title: Pandora's Jar
puzzles.flavor: Paint chips left behind at Delphi. The labels matter more than the colours.
hints: Each hex colour code is three ASCII bytes.
To check you're on track: the answer begins with H.

puzzles.title: The Judgement Of Paris
puzzles.flavor: Some numbers here are far too big for the alphabet. They're not too big for the periodic table.
hints: Each number is an atomic number. Write down each element's chemical symbol and read the symbols together as one word.
To check you're on track: the answer begins with C.

puzzles.title: Ambrosia
puzzles.flavor: A familiar grid, an unfamiliar alphabet.
hints: Sudoku using the letters shown instead of digits (each row, column and box uses each letter once). Read the numbered squares in order.
To check you're on track: the answer begins with N.

meta.title: Meta: The Oracle Is Closed
meta.flavor: Everything at Delphi has a place, and every place is exactly the right size.
hints: Each answer fits exactly one row of the grid by length; the shaded squares, top to bottom, spell the final answer.
To check you're on track: the final answer begins with O.
